title: Without Cancer, Taiwanese Would Live 3.7 Years Longer
summaryZh: 內政部：若排除癌症死亡，國人平均壽命可增3.7歲。
summaryHi: ताइवान: कैंसर से मौतें न हों तो औसत आयु 3.7 साल बढ़ सकती है।
summaryEs: Sin las muertes por cáncer, la esperanza de vida en Taiwán subiría 3,7 años.
summaryJa: がん死亡を除くと台湾の平均寿命は3.7年延びると内政部が発表。
summaryKo: 대만 내정부 "암 사망 제외하면 기대수명 3.7년 늘어".
summaryEn: Taiwan's average life expectancy would rise by 3.7 years if no one died of cancer, the interior ministry says.
paragraphs: Taiwan's average life expectancy would increase by 3.7 years if deaths from cancer were excluded, according to figures released by the Ministry of the Interior on Saturday.

To measure the impact of different illnesses, the ministry recalculated life expectancy with each of the 10 leading causes of death removed and compared the results with the overall average. The larger the gap, the greater the effect of that cause.
Average life expectancy in 2025 stood at 81.27 years. Without cancer deaths, it would climb to 84.97 years. Removing heart disease would add 1.54 years, while removing pneumonia would add 1.13 years.

Cancer has topped the list of causes of death for 44 consecutive years, claiming 54,838 lives in 2025, or 27.48 percent of the total. Even so, its impact appears to be easing: the difference has narrowed from 4.10 years in 2015 to 3.70 years.

Men lost more years than women to most of the leading causes, with diabetes, high blood pressure and kidney disease being the exceptions. Accidents reduced male life expectancy by 0.75 years, compared with 0.36 years for women, a gap the ministry linked to differences in occupation, physiology, diet, health care and lifestyle.
In Taiwan, people live for about 81 years on average. This number is from 2025.
The government asked a question: how long would people live if no one died of cancer? The answer is almost 85 years. That is 3.7 years more.
Cancer is the biggest cause of death in Taiwan. It has been number one for 44 years. In 2025, almost 55,000 people died of cancer. That is more than one in four deaths.
Heart disease is second. Without it, people would live about one and a half years longer.
There is some good news. Ten years ago, the number for cancer was 4.1 years. Now it is 3.7 years, so cancer is a little less deadly than before.
Taiwan's average life expectancy would rise by 3.7 years if cancer deaths were removed from the figures, the Ministry of the Interior said in a new report on Saturday.
The ministry took each of the 10 main causes of death and worked out how long people would live without it. The bigger the difference, the bigger the effect of that cause on life expectancy.
In 2025, average life expectancy was 81.27 years. Without cancer, it would reach 84.97 years. Without heart disease, people would live 1.54 years longer, and without pneumonia, 1.13 years longer.

Cancer has been Taiwan's leading cause of death for 44 years in a row. It killed 54,838 people in 2025, or about 27 percent of all deaths. However, its effect is getting slightly smaller: in 2015, the gap was 4.1 years.
Men lost more years than women to most causes. For example, accidents cost men 0.75 years but women only 0.36 years. The ministry said work, diet, lifestyle and health care may explain this.
Taiwan's average life expectancy would increase by 3.7 years if deaths from cancer were excluded, according to figures released by the Ministry of the Interior on Saturday.

To measure the impact of different illnesses, the ministry recalculated life expectancy with each of the 10 leading causes of death removed and compared the results with the overall average. The larger the gap, the greater the effect of that cause.
Average life expectancy in 2025 stood at 81.27 years. Without cancer deaths, it would climb to 84.97 years. Removing heart disease would add 1.54 years, while removing pneumonia would add 1.13 years.

Cancer has topped the list of causes of death for 44 consecutive years, claiming 54,838 lives in 2025, or 27.48 percent of the total. Even so, its impact appears to be easing: the difference has narrowed from 4.10 years in 2015 to 3.70 years.

Men lost more years than women to most of the leading causes, with diabetes, high blood pressure and kidney disease being the exceptions. Accidents reduced male life expectancy by 0.75 years, compared with 0.36 years for women, a gap the ministry linked to differences in occupation, physiology, diet, health care and lifestyle.
Eliminating cancer deaths would lengthen the average Taiwanese lifespan by 3.7 years, the Ministry of the Interior estimated on Saturday in an analysis of the country's leading causes of death.

The ministry gauged each illness's toll by recalculating life expectancy with one of the 10 principal causes stripped out and comparing the outcome with the actual average; the wider the gap, the heavier the burden that cause imposes.
Life expectancy in 2025 stood at 81.27 years, a figure that would rise to 84.97 without cancer. Heart disease and pneumonia trailed some way behind, accounting for 1.54 and 1.13 years respectively.

Cancer has been the foremost cause of death for 44 years running, claiming 54,838 lives last year, or 27.48 percent of all fatalities. Nevertheless, its grip seems to be loosening slightly, with the gap shrinking from 4.10 years a decade earlier to 3.70 years.

Men forfeited more years than women to most causes, diabetes, hypertensive disease and kidney disease aside. Accidental injuries alone shaved 0.75 years off male life expectancy, roughly double the female figure, a disparity the ministry attributed to occupation, physiology, diet, health care and lifestyle.

According to new estimates from the Ministry of the Interior, Taiwanese life expectancy would increase by 3.7 years if cancer were removed as a cause of death, underscoring the disease's substantial demographic impact.

The methodology involved recalculating average lifespan with each of the 10 leading causes excluded in turn and then comparing the outcome with the actual figure. Consequently, a larger discrepancy indicates a more significant contribution to mortality.

In 2025, average life expectancy was 81.27 years, whereas the hypothetical figure without cancer reached 84.97 years. By comparison, excluding heart disease and pneumonia would add 1.54 and 1.13 years respectively.

Cancer has remained the predominant cause of death for 44 consecutive years, accounting for 54,838 deaths in 2025, or 27.48 percent of the total. Nonetheless, there are signs of gradual improvement, as the gap has contracted from 4.10 years in 2015 to 3.70 years.

Notably, men lost more years than women to the majority of causes, with diabetes, hypertensive disease and kidney disease the only exceptions. Accidental injuries cost men 0.75 years compared with 0.36 years for women, a disparity the ministry attributed to differences in occupation, physiology, diet, health care and lifestyle.

reached.ex: Sales reached a record high last year.

recalculated.ex: The bank recalculated the interest on my loan.

recalculating.ex: Recalculating the budget took all afternoon.

reduced.ex: The shop reduced its prices this week.

remained.ex: The shop remained open all night.

removed.ex: All the trees were removed from the car park.

report.ex: The report was published on Friday.

respectively.en: in the same order as just mentioned
respectively.ex: Tom and Ann are 10 and 12 respectively.

results.ex: The test results came out today.

rise.ex: Rivers may rise after heavy rain.

row.en: in a row: one after another
row.ex: They won five games in a row.

running.en: one after another without a break
running.ex: It rained for five days running.

said.ex: She said the shop was closed.

second.ex: This is my second visit to Paris.

seems.ex: It seems the rain has stopped.

shaved.ex: The new train shaved ten minutes off the journey.

significant.en: large or important enough to notice
significant.ex: There was a significant rise in prices.

signs.en: things that show something is happening
signs.ex: There are signs that prices are falling.

so.ex: It was raining, so we stayed home.

some.en: an amount that is not exact; quite a lot

stood.ex: Unemployment stood at five per cent.

stripped.ex: Stripped of power, the town was dark.

substantial.ex: The new road needs a substantial amount of money.

note.meaning: 大量的；重大的。文中指癌症對人口壽命的顯著影響。
note.usage: IELTS 常用來取代 big/large：a substantial impact/increase/sum。

example.en: The new policy had a substantial impact on prices.
example.zh: 新政策對價格產生了重大影響。

noteHi.meaning: मात्रा या महत्व में बड़ा; काफ़ी।
noteHi.usage: big की जगह: a substantial impact/increase।
noteHi.exampleTr: नई नीति का कीमतों पर काफ़ी असर पड़ा।

noteEs.meaning: grande en cantidad o importancia; considerable.
noteEs.usage: En lugar de big: a substantial impact.
noteEs.exampleTr: La nueva política tuvo un impacto considerable en los precios.

noteJa.meaning: 量や重要性が大きい；相当な。
noteJa.usage: big の代わりに a substantial impact/increase。
noteJa.exampleTr: 新政策は価格に大きな影響を与えた。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 정책은 가격에 상당한 영향을 미쳤다.

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

then.ex: First read the text, then answer the questions.

there.en: used to say that something exists

toll.en: the harm or loss caused by something
toll.ex: Stress takes a heavy toll on health.

took.en: chose or picked something to deal with
took.ex: The teacher took each answer and checked it.

topped.ex: Cork topped the list of busy hospitals.

total.ex: The total cost was two million.

trailed.en: were behind others in a list or competition
trailed.ex: The team trailed by two goals at half-time.

underscoring.en: showing clearly that something is important
underscoring.ex: The figures came out, underscoring the problem.

note.meaning: 強調、凸顯（某事的重要性）。
note.usage: 常以分詞構句放句尾：…, underscoring the need/impact…；同義 underlining、highlighting。

example.en: Prices rose again, underscoring the need for action.
example.zh: 價格再度上漲，凸顯採取行動的必要。

noteEn.meaning: showing clearly that something is important or true.
noteEn.usage: Often a participle clause at the end: '..., underscoring the need for...'.

noteHi.meaning: साफ़ दिखाना कि कुछ महत्वपूर्ण या सच है।
noteHi.usage: वाक्य के अंत में: ..., underscoring the need for ...।
noteHi.exampleTr: कीमतें फिर बढ़ीं, जिससे कार्रवाई की ज़रूरत उजागर हुई।

noteEs.meaning: mostrar claramente que algo es importante.
noteEs.usage: Al final de la frase: ..., underscoring the need for...
noteEs.exampleTr: Los precios volvieron a subir, lo que subraya la necesidad de actuar.

noteJa.meaning: 重要性をはっきり示す；浮き彫りにする。
noteJa.usage: 文末の分詞構文：..., underscoring the need for ...
noteJa.exampleTr: 価格が再び上がり、対策の必要性が浮き彫りになった。

noteKo.usage: 문장 끝 분사구문: ..., underscoring the need for ...
noteKo.exampleTr: 가격이 또 올라 대책의 필요성이 부각됐다.

way.en: a distance or amount (some way behind = quite far behind)
way.ex: The second team was some way behind.

were.ex: The shops were closed on Sunday.

wider.ex: This is part of a wider plan.

women.ex: More women now work in science.

worked.ex: She worked out the total cost.

would.ex: A new park would help the town.
